shape.$description: Brand-specific geometry from the Alix Brand Guidelines (Jan 2026) 'Graphic Elements'. These are the forms that make a screen look like Alix rather than like a generic app, and nothing else in the system encodes them. Two families: the SHEER (wayfinding, p62–63) and the CONTAINER/CARD construction rules (p56–60).

sheer.$description: The sheered rectangle — 'Inspired by the lines of the Symbol, we've created sheered rectangles to be used throughout the brand' (p63). The book applies it to timeline steps, category tabs, segmented on/off controls and CTA buttons. It is the single most recognizable Alix UI form and must not be approximated with a plain rounded rect.

angle.$description: Degrees off vertical for the sheered edge, measured from the Symbol's chevron. Positive leans the top edge forward (reading direction).

inset.$description: Horizontal offset the sheer introduces across a standard control height (~40pt). Derived: round(height * tan(angle)). Used to overlap adjacent chips so they interlock rather than butt together.

overlap.$description: How far a following chip tucks under the previous one, so the seam reads as one continuous ribbon.

container.$description: The folder/tab container (p56–57). 'Alix's Settlement Specialists handle legal, financial, and personal details with clarity and organization… our brand utilizes a container system inspired by folders and tabs.' The tab is not decoration — it houses the label or CTA for the content inside.

radius-ratio.$description: Corner radius = 3% of the SHORTEST side of the container (p57, step 3). A 300pt-wide container gets 10pt. Proportional, not a fixed step — use shape.containerRadius() in code.

radius-min.$description: Floor for small containers, so a compact panel doesn't end up nearly square.

radius-max.$description: Ceiling on phone screens, so a full-bleed panel doesn't read as a pill.

grid-columns.$description: Vertical grid: tab width is set by dividing the container into 12 columns (p57, step 1). A tab is typically 4/12.

grid-rows.$description: Horizontal grid: split the height into 16 rows once the tab type size is set (p57, step 2).

tab-columns.$description: Default tab width in grid columns (the book's worked example is 1/4 of the width).

tab-padding.$description: Padding inside the tab (p57's worked example).

card.$description: The Card system (p58–60) — 'to call out notifications, features, and capabilities… can be overlaid on imagery'. Cards differ from containers: no tab, heavier corner rounding, and they are designed to overlap each other and photography.

margin-ratio.$description: Inner margin = 10% of the shortest side (p60, step 1).

margin-ratio-tight.$description: 18% 'for extreme cases' — very small cards, where 10% leaves the type touching the edge.

radius-ratio.$description: Corner radius as a fraction of the shortest side. Fitted to the book's worked examples: a 6x4 grid card rounds to 24 and a 6x6 to 30. Rounder than a container, which is what separates the two at a glance.
